repairs.reader_said: superlative-collision: claims the mild end of this family, and so do 1 sibling(s): peccable - at most one of these can hold
repairs.axis: merely liable to sin → wicked past any reform

synset_siblings.tone: Pictures reform as recovery and denies it — nothing here can be got back.
The heaviest of these four, since redemption is what it withholds: a final verdict rather than a prognosis.
The same refusal built on a blunt negative prefix, more workaday in sound than *irredeemable*.

whole_family.gloss: morally bad in principle or practice
whole_family.tone: The plain, unhedged moral verdict, and it covers both the settled principle and the actual practice rather than choosing between them.

whole_family.gloss: having the nature of vice
whole_family.tone: Names the thing as vice itself rather than describing a fault in it, which makes it absolute where *wicked* is merely damning.

whole_family.gloss: having the nature of vice
whole_family.tone: Presents vice as the settled bent of the thing, so it sounds like a diagnosis of character beside *evil*'s flat sentence.

whole_family.gloss: (of an actor or role) being or playing the villain
whole_family.tone: A casting word: it marks the villain's part, or the actor filling it, and condemns nobody.

whole_family.gloss: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
whole_family.tone: Formal and heavy-syllabled, delivering the same extreme-and-criminal verdict as *heinous* in a more elevated register.

whole_family.gloss: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
whole_family.tone: The blunt public condemnation, wickedness pitched so far into the criminal that the word works almost as a sentence.

whole_family.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
whole_family.tone: The gravest of its group, weighing the wrong as an enormity rather than simply logging it as sin like *sinful*.

whole_family.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
whole_family.tone: The plainest naming of wickedness-as-sin, condemnatory without the swell of *iniquitous*.

whole_family.gloss: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
whole_family.tone: Measures the wickedness as distance from godliness, so the fault is a standing away rather than *sinful*'s committed offence.

whole_family.gloss: insusceptible of reform
whole_family.tone: Pictures reform as recovery and denies it — nothing here can be got back.

whole_family.gloss: insusceptible of reform

whole_family.gloss: insusceptible of reform
whole_family.tone: The same refusal built on a blunt negative prefix, more workaday in sound than *irredeemable*.

whole_family.gloss: insusceptible of reform
whole_family.tone: The flattest of the group, stating only that reform will not take, with none of *irredeemable*'s note of lost salvation.

whole_family.gloss: extremely wicked
whole_family.tone: Condemns the wickedness in the abstract, where *villainous* points instead at the one committing it.

whole_family.gloss: extremely wicked
whole_family.tone: Casts the extreme wickedness as a villain's, making it a fact of character rather than of the deed.

whole_family.gloss: liable to sin
whole_family.tone: The mildest here by a wide margin: it concedes only that sin is possible, not that any has been done.
